resources.string: Install and manage skills, instructions and tool bundles
Install bundles of skills, instructions and connected tools.
Discover a starter pack or add a compatible bundle from npm, GitHub or your phone.
Changes apply to the next Code run. Existing runs keep their captured configuration.
Search npm packages tagged androidharness-plugin. Community results are not verified by AndroidHarness; compatibility is checked before installation.
No matching packages found. You can also add a package name, GitHub repository or local bundle.
Enter a package name, exact version or tag, such as @team/plugin@latest. The package must contain an AndroidHarness bundle.
Enter a GitHub repository. Optionally choose a branch, tag, commit or plugin subfolder. Your connected GitHub account can provide access to private repositories.
Import a ZIP, .tar.gz, .tgz or plugin folder. A folder containing SKILL.md can also be imported as a skill bundle.
%1$s installed. Its additions apply to the next Code run.
This removes the plugin from future runs. Your project files, hand-written configuration and unrelated settings are preserved.
Local MCP servers require a compatible app runtime. They start only through the existing approval flow.
Package installation scripts are never run by the installer. Plugin hooks use the isolated JavaScript runtime.
Skills and instructions become available when enabled. MCP servers and executable hooks keep their separate project-tool approval. Installation does not start servers.
This stops loading installed plugins. Your project files and other settings stay unchanged. Reinstall the plugins you want afterward.
A code-review skill and instructions for reporting verified findings.
